claims.quote: I set the oil lamp six feet from the mantel and propped the wick so the flame rode roughly eighteen inches above the hearth.
claims.value: six feet from mantel; flame 18 in above hearth

claims.quote: I measured the six feet again because measuring was the part of this that felt like control, then I pencilled a small cross on the floor seven inches to the left of the mirror’s centre and taped a strip of envelope paper there to hold the mark.
claims.value: mark seven inches left of mirror centre on parlor floor

claims.quote: The seam in the silvering caught it first and, for a heartbeat that was both longer and too short, the glass answered with an intensified shimmer along that hairline joint.
claims.value: intensified shimmer along hairline seam under lamp activation

claims.quote: My hand in front of the glass registered a fraction of a second sooner than its reflection — the lag I'd written down as a prediction —
claims.value: reflection lag of fraction of a second between real movement and reflection

claims.quote: The reflection was not the room I was sitting in. In the glass the narrow stair descended on the left while, behind me, the real stair rose on the right. Light in the mirror had a colder edge, a blue that did not belong to my lamp; the reflected banister cast a shadow where the real banister made none.
claims.value: reflected parlor shows stair descending on left (real stair rises on right) and bluish, colder light source in reflection

claims.quote: Tucked into the margin, dated March 24, 1972, were three short directives I read aloud, as if hearing them aloud would make them obey me as well as the paper:
"Place the flame where the sill is cut."
claims.value: Place the flame where the sill is cut.

claims.quote: "Speak her name and give the leaving."
claims.value: Speak her name and give the leaving.

claims.quote: I took the brass key from the mantel—still dull where my thumb had warmed it earlier—and turned it in the attic hatch's rim lock.
claims.value: used to open attic hatch rim lock

claims.quote: A single slat on the north rafter was split from edge to edge and left a vertical gap of about two inches. It sat two feet from the hatch and ten feet from the east-facing window, and when I knelt on the hatch lip a thin shaft of lamp-light threaded through the gap and struck the attic floor in a line that aimed back toward the mantel.
claims.value: split slat on north rafter, vertical 2-inch gap, located 2 ft from hatch, 10 ft from east window; admits shaft aimed toward mantel

claims.quote: The stair to the attic was narrow and pitched; I climbed into a low, cedar-dark space where dust made the air taste like dry paper. The attic ceiling brushed my forearms; the roof slants made the room feel smaller than the house below.
claims.value: low cedar-dark attic, narrow pitched stair, low ceiling that brushes forearms

claims.quote: Hannah came then — not a storm but a sequence: she tapped once, twice, three times along the inside of the frame; she did it in precise, patient counts, as if enumerating steps. Her mouth formed one slow word. I read it because there is no other polite thing to do with an apparition that mouths a syllable: "light."
claims.value: communicates by tapping and mouthing single logical words (example: 'light')

claims.quote: In the mirror's other side the dust seemed to part where her finger slid; in that reflected seam the darkened trail spelled a single word: "free." The dust on my side of the frame did not move.
claims.value: the word 'free' appeared only in the mirror's reflected surface; no physical dust moved on Lena's side

claims.quote: I struck it, lifted the flame to the wick, and said, plainly, "Hannah Hale." Then I read the diary line and spoke it aloud to the room, slow and deliberate: "Speak her name and give the leaving."
claims.value: spoke Hannah Hale's name aloud and read 'Speak her name and give the leaving' while bringing the match flame to the wick
